About Blog Projects

Projects

Events at NJIT

I realized that the method by which students can learn about events at NJIT is rather Archean. So, I’m currently working on an iOS app that I hope solves for this! The app will be paired with a Twitter Bot and a Public API for events. Source code is available on GitHub: iOS | API. Follow us @EventsAtNJIT on Twitter. Questions / Comments / Concerns? Email us at njit.events.app@gmail.com.

Software Developers’ Network

Software Developers’ Network, or SDN for short, was one of my first extensive webapps that authenticated users for secure pages and allowed for interaction in the form of posts and comments. Frontend built with Bootstrap. Check a live version of the app out here, via which you can also learn more about the tech stack! Code is publicly available via GitHub.

Midloc

Midloc was my first iOS app, via which I learned a multitude of frontend and backend concepts. Check out the app on the iTunes App Store, and learn more about my experience here.

Hackathons

Spring 2016

PennApps

We built Storyteller. Teamed up with Sakib Jalal, Alec Huang and Ema Tasmin to create this location-based social app which is a spin on Humans of New York. As you make your way through your city throughout the day, you miss so many chances to connect with the incredible people around you. If they’re not featured on HoNY for being ordinary people leading extraordinary lives, we’ll never hear their story. Our app connects you with those you pass by every day, giving you a chance to learn about who you’ve passed by throughout the day. Be inspired - it may encourage you to stop and say hey more often! Worked on the iOS App with Alec and Ema. Source code is available on GitHub.

Dragon Hacks

We built Pay Park - winners of the Best Use of Amazon Web Services hack! Teamed up with Sakib Jalal, Alec Huang and Varun Shah to build this iOS App that has two components: an API for city governments to populate our database with street parking availability throughout their city in a standardized way, and a client-facing API that allows users to find, select and pay for street parking all from an app. Gone are the days of parking meters and kiosks. Worked on the iOS App with Alec. Source code is available on GitHub.

Fall 2015

YHack

We built fnActivists. Teamed up with Jeet Patel to build this iOS App based on the Fiscal Note, which delivered an exhausting amount of government and legislative data. Wrote the Python Flask server that interacted with the API, managed user data in MySQL and served a controlled amount of data to the iOS Client. The app displayed data to users in a visual way, allowed users to set reminders for tags that related to their political interests, and more. Source code is available on GitHub.

BostonHacks

We built Tonifai. Teamed up with Varun Shah and Ananth Rao to build this Twilio-based app that “converted” your friends’ Contacts image on your phone into a tune, called them and “sang” it to them. Wrote the iOS App that sent a request to a server, along with the friend’s contact information and image, to place a phone call through Twilio.

HackUMass

I built Google Notepad, a Google Chrome extension that gives you a textarea when you search “notepad” in Google Search. After typing in your quick note, pressing enter sends the email to the account you’re logged in with using Mandrill. Source code is available on GitHub.

We built Bump It Up. Teamed up with Dylan Lesko and Ashton Welles to build this iOS app that detected road conditions using the built in accelerometer. This data was sent to a server side Flask app that identified major variaances in the data as potential potholes or bad road conditions. Constructed a public-facing API that other developers can use to consume our user-generated data. Source code is available on GitHub.

Post-Exams Stress Hack!

I built “Guess That Number!”, a post-exam stress hack. This Twilio-based app replicates the “What number am I thinking of?” game! Guess a number and text it to +1 (908) 360-5009! A Flask app manages contests and contestants in a SQLite database. Every time someone wins, a new contest is launched. Give it a try! Source code is available on GitHub.

HackRU

We built VSE - Virtual Stock Exchange. Teamed up with first time hackers Krupa Patel, Jey Shah and Richard Vo to build this introductory-type web application. Built the NodeJS, ExpressJS and MongoDB RESTful API - my first exposure to these technologies.

hackNY

We built Rubik’s Hacks. Teamed up with Ismail Mustafa to build a Rubik’s Cube solver. Built the iOS app that took pictures of each side and wrote a rudimentary client-side image processing algorithm in Swift that identified the colors at 80% - 90% accuracy. Easily the most challenging hack I’ve been a part of thus far!

HopHacks

We built CommunityHelps. Teamed up with Varun Shah and Joseph Suria to create this app, where folks can ask their community members for help on tasks. We took on the daring challenge of building a RESTful API, iOS app, Android app and Web app all in one hackathon. Unfortunately we didn’t finish, but our experience was incredible.

PennApps

We built Find My Health - winners of the Best Social Innovation Hack! Teamed up with Haitham Maaieh, Viral Jogani and Dean Rexines to create this healthcare hack. Built the RESTful API for this iOS app.

We were featured in Rutgers University’s student newspaper, The Daily Targum! Check out our article here.

Summer 2015

Angelhack Manhattan

We built Myodrums - winners of the Best Myoband Hack! Teamed up with Ismail Mustafa, Malcolm Jones and Brandon Max to build a virtual drumset. Helped with iOS and analyzed Myoband data for each drum stroke.

Angelhack Brooklyn

We built Sentimatch. Teamed up with Pranav Dhar, Ismail Mustafa, and Anas Bouzoubaa to make a location-based social app. Contributed by reading tons of documentation and helping our iOS developers, Ismail and Anas, with the product! Incredible first hackathon experience.
